Alex — great to chat. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps below (attaching the short SLO spreadsheet).

Recap of SLOs (as I heard them):
- target p95 latency <= 250ms for short prompts (~50 tokens)
- streaming: first-token < 150ms, streaming of longer outputs (~250 tokens)
- concurrency: peak ~40 concurrent requests, sustained ~20 reqs/s
- throughput: ~1k tokens/sec during peak
- initial cost target: ~ $8k/mo

Redwood levers we typically use to hit this mix of latency and cost:
1) Continuous batching: auto-batching with tight latency SLOs; helps reduce tokens/second cost while keeping p95 low if configured with dynamic batch cutoffs.
2) Prefix/KV caching: for repeated prompts/seeded system messages — large wins for chat-style workloads.
3) Quantization profiles: Q4_0 or Q4_K_M variants (4-bit) can reduce GPU memory and cost with modest latency changes; larger models quantized to Q4 often permit higher throughput on same hardware.
4) Model variants & smart routing: smaller low-latency models for short queries, fall back to a higher-quality quantized variant for longer or high-quality flows.
5) Dedicated pools + burst capacity: reserve capacity for peak windows to guarantee p95s and use burst for spikes.

Proposed next steps:
- Priyom (SE) to provide a short cost/latency tradeoff matrix with recommended model/quantization + estimated infra config (batch size, concurrency per GPU, expected p95).
- We'll include a canary plan: start on a small % of traffic in Dedicated or Private, run latency + regression evals, then expand.
- Follow-up call: Tue 2026-03-31 10:00am PT — confirm?

Attaching: SLO_requirements_acme_v0.pdf

Thanks, Marissa — I put together an initial assessment below (short summary in body; attached is a rough cost calc workbook).

Short technical summary / recommendations to meet the targets:
- Target p95 <= 250ms (short prompts): achievable with a mix of small low-latency model for short-turns + quantized mid-size model for longer outputs. Example config: 13B quantized (Q4) for most queries, 70B quantized as fallback for high-quality or long generations.
- Streaming first-token <150ms: Requires aggressive prefix streaming and a dedicated low-latency routing path (hot path). Achievable with Dedicated pools sized for concurrency. If using Hosted, use a low-latency tier with prewarmed workers and continuous batching thresholds tuned low.
- Continuous batching: set dynamic batch cutoffs at ~4-8ms for UX-sensitive short queries; this keeps p95 low while still achieving batching benefits during sustained demand. Batching primarily reduces $/token at higher throughput.
- KV/prefix caching: recommended for your ~30% identical prompts — expect 20-40% token reduction depending on prompt length and cache hit rate. Cache can be ephemeral (in-memory) for privacy-compliant setups; persistent caching is available only with customer consent and KMS encryption.
- Quantization profiles: Q4_0 and Q4_1 provide good memory/throughput tradeoffs. We recommend starting on Q4 for 13B; test quality regression with your eval set.
- Smart routing & concurrency knobs: route short queries to small model instances with per-request early-exit heuristics; route long/high-quality jobs to quantized mid/large models. Set per-GPU concurrency to match model and batch tuning (we'll provide numbers per GPU).

Estimated cost pointers (very rough):
- Hosted (low-latency tier, Q4 13B): ~$0.20 / 1k tokens (after batching & caching) — rough
- Dedicated (reserved 4x A100-equivalents, quantized): amortized cost closer to ~$0.12 / 1k tokens at your scale but requires commit/reserve

Attachments: approx_cost_calc_acme.xlsx (contains scenario tabs: hosted-fast, dedicated-quantized, canary)

Privacy note: prefix caching can be configured as ephemeral in-memory only; persistent caches use customer KMS and strict retention policies. We'll include the policy text in the next doc.

I'll add a small table with expected p95 numbers by config for the call.

Priyom
